newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA NAME 30-MAN SQUAD FOR EUROPE TOUR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA NAME 30-MAN SQUAD FOR EUROPE TOUR.

text.p: The Australian Rugby Union (ARU)
on Wednesday named five uncapped players in a 30-man squad for
its eight-week tour of Europe but gave no clear indication
whether a test against England would be included.
Australia arrive in Italy on October 15 at the start of a
tour which also includes tests against Ireland, Scotland and
Wales.
The ARU had hoped an England test would be added to the
British leg of its tour so the Wallabies could play their first
"Grand Slam" of matches against the four home unions since 1984.
Australia first suggested December 7 as the date for the
England test but the Four Home Unions Tour Committee rejected
that date because it clashed with a scheduled match against the
Barbarians.
The ARU last week suggested either November 2 or 16 as
alternative dates for the England test and said they would
consider cancelling the December 1 test against Wales at Cardiff
if those dates were rejected.
Australia had added the test against Wales to their original
tour schedule after a request from Welsh officials.
"A test against England at Twickenham is still a possibility
and an announcement is expected in the next few days," a
statement released by the ARU said.
Australia coach Greg Smith told reporters the squad would be
increased to 32 if the England test goes ahead, with test
forwards Tim Gavin and Ewen McKenzie the players to be added.
Gavin and McKenzie were overlooked when selectors announced
their squad, which includes uncapped forwards Andrew Blades,
Mark Connors, David Giffin, Toutai Kefu and Brett Robinson.
All five featured this year in the inaugural Super 12
tournament for provincial teams from Australia, New Zealand and
South Africa.
The first test of the tour is against Italy in Padova on
October 23, a match that will mark David Campese's 100th
appearance in Australia's colours.
Campese in June increased his world record for tries scored
in internationals to 64 by crossing in a one-off test against
Canada in Brisbane.
Squad: John Eales (captain), Andrew Blades, Michael Brial,
Matthew Burke, David Campese, Marco Caputo, Mark Connors, Dan
Crowley, Michael Foley, David Giffin, George Gregan, Richard
Harry, Andrew Heath, Daniel Herbert, Tim Horan, Pat Howard,
Toutai Kefu, David Knox, Stephen Larkham, Jason Little, Daniel
Manu, Garrick Morgan, Sam Payne, Brett Robinson, Joe Roff,
Richard Tombs, Ben Tune, Tim Wallace, John Welborn, David
Wilson.
